Replacing the strongest conv on the final edge with a parameter-free pool removes substantial learned capacity.
Adding a skip where edge 0 was empty reconnects node 1 and revives downstream paths through edges 2 and 4.
Creating a direct conv input->output path where none existed helps far more than swapping an existing op.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a 3x3 conv adds a new parametric path, unlike replacing an existing conv.
Upgrading a parameter-free skip to a 3x3 conv adds capacity, while replacing a conv yields little change.
Without the direct input->output edge, the node-2 path carries more of the signal, so degrading it to pooling hurts more.
Removing a 3x3 conv into the output loses capacity, whereas removing a skip or pool can be neutral or beneficial.
If node 2 has no input from node 1, removing edge 1 makes node 2 dead and also nullifies edge 5.
With node 1 disconnected, edge 3 carries most of the output, so turning it into a pool costs much more.

raw:
Based on the 100 experiments and how NAS-Bench-201 cells are wired, these are the 10 interaction hypotheses I believe hold:

1. **Edge 3 → none, when edge 4 is none: lower.** If node 1 has no direct path to the output, removing the input→output edge cuts off more of the remaining routes. Experiment 98 is the clearest case.
2. **Edge 5 → avg_pool_3x3, when edge 5 is nor_conv_3x3: lower.** Swapping the strongest conv on the last edge into the output for a parameter-free pool removes much of the cell's learned capacity. See experiment 71.
3. **Edge 0 → skip_connect, when edge 0 is none: higher.** This edit reconnects node 1, which was disconnected, so whole downstream paths come back to life. See experiments 50, 61 and 99.
4. **Edge 3 → nor_conv_1x1, when edge 3 is none: higher.** Adding a direct conv path where there was none helps far more than replacing an existing op. See experiment 95.
5. **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3, when edge 5 is none: higher.** Filling an empty edge into the output gives large gains (experiments 1 and 77). Replacing an existing conv gives about zero (45 and 92).
6. **Edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3, when edge 4 is skip_connect: higher.** Upgrading a skip to a conv adds capacity (experiments 4 and 19). Replacing a 1x1 conv changes little (63).
7. **Edge 2 → avg_pool_3x3, when edge 3 is none: lower.** Without the direct input→output edge, the path through node 2 carries more of the signal, so degrading it hurts more. See experiment 100.
8. **Edge 5 → none, when edge 5 is nor_conv_3x3: lower.** Removing a 3x3 conv into the output loses capacity (experiment 39). Removing a skip or pool can even help (experiment 18).
9. **Edge 1 → none, when edge 2 is none: lower.** If node 2 has no input from node 1, removing edge 1 leaves node 2 dead, which effectively removes edge 5 as well.
10. **Edge 3 → avg_pool_3x3, when edge 0 is none: lower.** With node 1 disconnected, edge 3 carries most of the output, so replacing it with a pool costs much more (experiments 16 and 31 versus 12, 25 and 60).
